title: The Only Bird With a Beak Longer Than Its Body Can't Preen With It
subject: sword-billed hummingbird

scenes.text: One bird's beak is longer than the rest of it.
The sword-billed hummingbird of the Andes. Its bill is about ten centimetres, four inches, longer than its body, tail not counted.
It weighs about twelve grams and can't reach its own feathers. So it grooms itself with its feet.
At rest it tilts its head back and holds the bill almost straight up, or it would tip forward.
The reason is one flower. A passionflower with a nectar tube about as long as that bill. Only this bird reaches the bottom.
The flower feeds one bird. One bird pollinates the flower. A beak too long for everything, except the one thing that matters.

description:
The sword-billed hummingbird is the only bird whose beak is longer than its body (not counting the tail), about 10 centimetres on a bird that weighs around 12 grams.
It cannot preen with its bill, so it grooms with its feet, and it rests with the bill tilted upward to stay balanced. The bill evolved alongside Passiflora mixta, a passionflower whose nectar tube is roughly as long, so the two depend on each other.
What other animal is built around a single food?
first_comment: If that flower disappeared, the bird would have nothing its beak fits. Which animal do you think is the most over-specialised?
